criterios: This question resolves YES if, in the Denver Broncos vs. Seattle Seahawks game scheduled for Thursday, October 15, 2026, Denver quarterback Bo Nix is credited with 250 or more passing yards in the official NFL box score for that game. It resolves NO if he is credited with fewer than 250 passing yards, including if he does not play. Resolution is based on Bo Nix's 2026 game log on ESPN (https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/stats/_/id/4426338/bo-nix) for the Week 6 game, the official NFL.com box score, or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). For example, a stat line of 251 passing yards resolves YES; 249 passing yards resolves NO.
letra_pequena: "Passing yards" refers to the standard NFL passing-yards statistic for the quarterback as recorded in the official box score. If the game is postponed or rescheduled to a later date, resolution is based on the game whenever it is actually played. If the game is cancelled entirely and not played, the question is annulled.

**(a) Time left:** The game is Thursday, October 15, 2026, about 10 days away. The outcome will be known that night.

**(b) Status quo:** Nix averages about 205 yards per game this season and has reached 250 once in four games. Seattle's pass defense ranks first in the league, and none of its four opponents has passed for 190 yards. If nothing changes, the likely outcome is No.

**(c) Reference class and base rate:**
- Nix reached 250+ in about 34% of his career regular-season starts (13 of 38).
- League-wide, about 25–30% of QB starts reach 250.
- In Thursday games, Nix went 1 for 4.
- In his only game against Seattle, he threw for 138 yards.

Several factors pull his chances below the base rate:
- His 2026 form is down at 6.1 yards per attempt.
- He is on a short week after the Chargers game.
- Courtland Sutton's workload is being limited and Pat Bryant's ankle is a question.
- Seattle has been elite at stopping passes, allowing 95–189 yards per game and the fewest explosive plays in the league.

A likely prop line of about 200–210 with a standard deviation of about 60 implies roughly 20–23% for 250+. The matchup-specific evidence pushes that a bit lower.

**(d) No scenario:** Seattle limits explosive plays and Denver leans on the run and short passes to RJ Harvey. Nix finishes around 170–220 yards, as other QBs have against Seattle this season.

**(e) Yes scenario:** Denver falls behind early against the champions and must pass a lot, say 40+ attempts. Alternatively, a change of play-caller to Sean Payton sparks the offense and Waddle or Sutton break a couple of long plays. Either path could push Nix to 255 or more.

**(f) Technicalities:**
- The threshold is gross passing yards, so sacks are not subtracted.
- If Nix does not play or leaves early, the question resolves No.
- If the game is postponed, it still counts whenever it is played.
- There is no meaningful ambiguity in how this resolves.
